title: Digestive tract anatomy: stomach and intestines
description: The gastrointestinal tract from oesophagus to rectum, with the villus that does the absorbing.

questions.question: What happens to food in the stomach and intestines?
questions.answer: The stomach stores and mixes food with acid and enzymes. The small intestine completes much digestion and absorbs nutrients; the large intestine absorbs water and forms stool.

questions.question: How long is the route through the digestive tract?
questions.answer: Food moves from oesophagus to stomach, small intestine and large intestine before leaving through the rectum and anal canal. Length varies between people and measurement methods.

questions.question: What is the oesophagus?
questions.answer: A 25 cm muscular tube from pharynx to stomach, passing through the diaphragm at T10. Function: Propels the bolus by peristalsis; the lower sphincter prevents reflux.

questions.question: Where is the body of stomach located?
questions.answer: The main reservoir between fundus and antrum, lined by acid- and pepsin-secreting mucosa with rugae. Function: Mixes food with acid and pepsin; intrinsic factor for B12 absorption is made here.

questions.question: What is the function of the rugae?
questions.answer: Function: Allow expansion and channel the flow of chyme. Longitudinal folds of gastric mucosa that flatten as the stomach distends.
